evals.setup: A small Python repo with pytest, a git history of about 40 commits, and no GitHub remote. src/billing/invoice.py changed in 12 commits, 3 with 'fix:' subjects that touched no test, and no test imports it. tests/test_orders.py mocks src/orders/repo.py (an owned module) and asserts save() call order; 4 'refactor:' commits changed it. tests/test_cart.py and tests/test_checkout.py both assert the same cart total. One test calls time.sleep(3). There is no coverage config and no CI.
expected_behavior: Times the full suite and a single test file and records both commands in a Vitals table
Runs scripts/test-history.py drift, fixes and refactors rather than hand-rolling git log pipelines
Files a blind-spot candidate for src/billing/invoice.py that names a seam with what it catches and misses, and cites the untested fix commits by SHA
Files a waste candidate for tests/test_orders.py that names the prune-tests category (tied to the implementation) and what still guards the behaviour
Reports the duplicated cart-total assertion and the sleep as waste with a cost
Does not add coverage tooling to the project

Writes docs/test-review/<date>-<slug>/README.md plus one card per candidate, adds the review to docs/test-review/README.md, commits them on a docs/test-review-<slug> branch, and stops there without implementing anything (opening the PR needs GitHub, which this setup lacks)

evals.setup: A TypeScript repo with vitest and no GitHub remote. Its newest report under docs/test-review/ is committed, with a status table whose batch the user already confirmed (C1 and C2 both `in-progress`): C1 (blind spot at parsePrice(input), behaviours: rejects negative amounts, rounds to cents) and C2 (waste: three tests in src/__tests__/format.test.ts asserting a private helper). parsePrice currently accepts negative amounts.
expected_behavior: Starts building C1 without asking the user to confirm the batch or the seam again, calling the Skill tool with tdd
For the rounding behaviour, which already passes, breaks the code temporarily to see the new test fail, reverts, and names the mutation in the commit body
Treats the negative-amount test failing against unchanged code as a live defect: keeps the test, fixes parsePrice in the same PR, and marks the row as a live defect
Calls the Skill tool with prune-tests for C2 and times the affected tests before and after
Builds C1 on test/<slug> and C2 on a branch cut from C1's, one commit series per candidate, and never merges (the PR steps need GitHub, which this setup lacks)
Leaves C1 and C2 `in-progress` in the committed status table rather than recording a PR, and reports that no PR was opened because there is no GitHub remote

evals.setup: A Python repo where src/payments/gateway.py builds its HTTP client inside charge() with no way to inject it, and the only tests patch gateway._build_client and gateway._sign. The suite runs on pre-commit via lefthook and takes 45 seconds.
expected_behavior: Lists gateway.py under Hand-offs with a /arch-review src/payments line instead of filing a blind-spot candidate that mocks internals
Files an infra candidate to move the 45-second suite from pre-commit to pre-push, routed through setup-lefthook
Does not file the tests patching gateway._build_client and gateway._sign as waste: with no seam to rewrite them at, they stay until /arch-review adds one, and the hand-off says so
Keeps the scan scoped to src/payments and says so in the report header

evals.setup: A TypeScript repo with vitest, with a local bare repo as origin (no GitHub remote). Its newest report under docs/test-review/ is committed. An earlier run built C1 and stopped at the candidate boundary: the status table has C1 `pr-open` on branch test/parse-price, and C2 `in-progress` (waste: three tests in src/__tests__/format.test.ts asserting a private helper, confirmed with the batch). Branch test/parse-price exists on origin.
expected_behavior: Reads C2's `in-progress` row as an already-confirmed batch and starts building C2 without asking the user to confirm again
Cuts C2's branch from C1's branch (test/parse-price), not from the default branch
Calls the Skill tool with prune-tests on C2's tests only and times them before and after
Updates C2's status row and never merges
